raw_response:
This year I farm like I done the past few years, just adjusting a bit based on what neighbors got last season.

My 12 mu — I keep 6 mu in wheat-maize rotation like always, that's my main food and sure money. The other 6 mu I split between vegetables for the market and stevia because the company buyer comes through and pays alright.

For wheat on the 6 mu — I plow after maize comes off in October, then put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before sowing, that's 100 jin each mu. Come spring when it starts jointing I broadcast one bag of urea, about 30 jin per mu. I water 3 times — once before winter, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu so I expect the same, maybe 500 kg.

For maize — after wheat harvest I don't plow, just direct seed with the machine. One bag compound at planting, then top-dress urea at big trumpet stage, about 40 jin. Water twice if rain is short. Spray once or twice for borer. Neighbors got 1100 jin per mu, I should do similar.

Vegetables — cabbage and cauliflower I put 1 mu each. These eat a lot of fertilizer. I spread 3 cart loads of chicken manure per mu, then 2 bags compound, and side-dress urea twice. Water many times — maybe 6-7. Spray for worms 4-5 times, these bugs are bad.

Chili and eggplant 1 mu each. Same as cabbage but more potassium because the fruit needs it. I plough deep, put manure, 2 bags compound, and drip water when I can. Spray 5 times — these get diseases easy.

Stevia 2 mu — this crop doesn't need much. One bag compound per mu, water 4 times, spray 2 times. The company gives us seedlings.

decision.reasoning_summary: I keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like always — that's my steady income and food. The other 6 mu I split between vegetables (cabbage, cauliflower, chili, eggplant, 1 mu each) and stevia (2 mu) because the vegetable market in town pays decent and the stevia company buys from us. I use the same fertilizer plan as last year — 2 bags of compound per mu for grain crops plus urea top-dress, more fertilizer and manure for vegetables since they eat a lot. I'd rather put a little extra urea than have yellow leaves and lose yield. I watch what my neighbors do, and my yields last year were solid so I keep it the same.
